messages:
Zara: quick follow-up from today's all-hands infra update — a few clarifying q's on regional bursting and autoscale playbook. TL;DR: which regions get reserved bursts vs. opportunistic pools?
Ken: good call. short answers: reserved bursts = enterprise regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1), opportunistic = all others for now. working doc linked in thread.
Varun: @Ken is that set in the autoscaler policy or routing layer? asking because some customers want predictable latency not just capacity.
Ken: routing layer. policy has a 'priority_tier' field. if priority_tier=enterprise -> route to reserved burst pool; else try opportunistic then fall back to shared.
Emily: can we get a sample policy snippet? would help SEs communicate to customers.
Ken: sure — example below:
```
priority_tier: enterprise
preferred_pools:
  - reserved-us-west-2
  - reserved-eu-west-1
fallback_pools:
  - opportunistic-global
  - shared-dedicated
max_burst_tokens: 1e6
```
Varun: perfect, thanks. followup: how do we measure "opportunistic" SLOs? we saw variance in last week's replay.
Ken: metric-wise: p95 latency & missed_tokens/sec per pool. ops-sre is adding a dashboard.
Ryan: action item — we should add a notify rule when missed_tokens/sec > 50 for >5m in an opportunistic pool. I'll make the pager proposal.
Emily: any ETA on making reserved bursts selectable per-account in the console? some customers asked for region pinning.
Ken: product/console team alpha next sprint (2 weeks) for per-account region allowance UI. backend gating is done.
Zara: thanks. one more ask from leadership Q: cost-controls during burst — do we cap spend automatically?
Ken: short: yes, there's a per-account burst cap field. default off for now, enabled for enterprise trials. we want to avoid surprise invoices — will add soft warning thresholds first.
Varun: will the cap block traffic or queue? we should queue and degrade to smaller models first.
Ken: current plan: cascade order = smaller-quantized-model -> queue -> reject. engineers can opt into cascade.
ops-bot: note: canary deploy scheduled: autoscaler v1.7 -> rollout to opportunistic pools at 02:00 UTC.
Emily: thanks @ops-bot. last logistics q: is there a migration window for customers pinned to eu-central-1 if we need to move reserved capacity?
Ken: yes, 30-day notice for any migration that affects reserved pools. we also provide transfer credits in most cases.
Zara: awesome. can someone post the linked doc + action items after this thread? copying @Ken @Ryan to own action items. :thumbsup:
Ryan: I'll post a short follow-up doc with the dashboard links + pager proposal by EOD.
Ken: I'll update the autoscale playbook with the policy snippet and add the per-account cap field notes.
Varun: will review playbook and share any SLO tweaks.
Zara: great work, team. closing thread — will circle back in next infra sync.
